- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is flat or rising slowly, reduce forecast slope to avoid over-optimism.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior period), model tends to overshoot — cap forecast growth to 3–5% per period to avoid overcorrection.
- If official event net supply is negative and sentiment is bearish, model often underestimates downside — add 1–2% downward bias to forecast mean.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model overfits to recent sentiment — smooth forecast with 3-period moving average to reduce noise.
- If recent auction supply events are frequent (≥3/30d), model tends to overreact — reduce forecast volatility by 15–20% to reflect market exhaustion.
- For 30d horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14d moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion trend.
- When bullish sentiment is high but true outcome is lower than forecast, model may be ignoring supply events — reduce forecast by 1–3% per event if supply net is negative.
